title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1 Art & Culture PART-5

questions.question: Shahid Parvez Khan, Budhaditya Mukherjee and Anoushka Shankar are associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Shahid Parvez Khan, Budhaditya Mukherjee, and Anoushka Shankar (daughter of Pt. Ravi Shankar) are all distinguished masters of the Sitar. They represent different Gharanas (schools) but are united by their virtuosity on this plucked string instrument.

Note: The Sitar is a mainstay of Hindustani Classical Music and is known for its long neck and sympathetic strings that create a shimmering sound.

questions.question: The musician Sivamani is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
Anandan Sivamani, popularly known as Sivamani, is a world-renowned percussionist associated with the Drums and various other percussion instruments. He is famous for his high-energy performances and his ability to create music using unconventional objects like water jugs and shells.

Fact: He has collaborated extensively with A.R. Rahman and was part of the musical group Silk.

questions.question: Who among the following is associated with the musical instrument Surbahar?
questions.solution:
Annapurna Devi (born Roshanara Khan) was a legendary musician associated with the Surbahar (bass sitar). She was the daughter of Allauddin Khan and the first wife of Pt. Ravi Shankar.

Instrument Note: The Surbahar is larger than a sitar and produces much deeper, lower-frequency sounds, making it ideal for the slow, meditative Dhrupad style of music.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities is associated with the musical instrument Mandolin?
questions.solution:
U. Srinivas was a child prodigy who achieved international fame for playing the Mandolin in the Carnatic Classical tradition. Before him, the mandolin was considered a Western folk instrument unsuitable for Indian ragas.

Legacy: He was often called 'Mandolin Srinivas' and received the Padma Shri at the age of 24.

questions.question: Identify the musician who is associated with musical instrument Sarod.
questions.solution:
Ustad Allauddin Khan was a multi-instrumentalist but is most celebrated as a master of the Sarod. He was the founder of the Maihar Gharana and the teacher of icons like Pt. Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan.

Note: The Sarod is a fretless string instrument with a metal fingerboard, known for its deep, resonant, and introspective tone.

questions.question: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ram Narayan is the musician single-handedly credited with elevating the Sarangi from an accompanying instrument to a solo concert instrument in Hindustani music.

Instrument Fact: The Sarangi is a bowed instrument carved from a single block of wood, traditionally used to accompany vocalists because its sound closely resembles the human voice.

questions.question: Who among the following is an exponent of the classical instrument, Santoor?
questions.solution:
Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was the pioneer who introduced the Santoor—originally a folk instrument from Jammu and Kashmir—to the world of Indian Classical Music.

Description: The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer with 72 to 100 strings, played with a pair of delicate wooden mallets called Kalam.

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of the musical instruments according to the given sequence of their associated personalities: Ustad Allah Rakha, Totaram Sharma, TH Vinayakam.
questions.solution:
The correct sequence matching the artists to their instruments is:
  • Ustad Allah Rakha: Tabla (The legendary partner of Pt. Ravi Shankar).
  • Totaram Sharma: Pakhawaj (A two-headed barrel drum used in Dhrupad).
  • TH Vinayakam: Ghatam (The earthenware pot percussion).

Note: T.H. 'Vikku' Vinayakam is a Grammy-winning artist famous for his lightning-fast rhythms on the pot.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian classical tabla players was called ‘Abbaji’? He collaborated with American jazz drummer Buddy Rich to create a music album in 1968.
questions.solution:
Ustad Alla Rakha was affectionately known as 'Abbaji' (he was also the father of Zakir Hussain). In 1968, he collaborated with jazz legend Buddy Rich on the ground-breaking album Rich à la Rakha, which blended Indian rhythms with Western Jazz.

Legacy: He belonged to the Punjab Gharana of Tabla playing.

questions.question: Which of the following awards was received by Pandit Birju Maharaj in 1986?
questions.solution:
Pandit Birju Maharaj, the face of the Lucknow 'Kalka-Bindadin' Gharana of Kathak, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (India's second-highest civilian award) in 1986.

Note: He was not only a dancer but also a talented vocalist, percussionist, and choreographer who brought Kathak to global prominence.

questions.question: Pandit Jasraj, Bhimsen Joshi and Zakir Hussain are associated with which form of music?
questions.solution:
Pandit Jasraj (Vocalist), Bhimsen Joshi (Vocalist), and Zakir Hussain (Tabla) are all stalwarts of Hindustani Classical Music, the traditional music of North India.

Note: Pt. Bhimsen Joshi was a recipient of the Bharat Ratna, and Zakir Hussain is a multi-Grammy winner.

questions.question: The famous musician, Faiyaz Khan is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
Ustad Faiyaz Khan was a towering figure of the Agra Gharana. While he was primarily one of the greatest classical vocalists of his time, he was also proficient in playing the Tabla and the harmonium.

Title: He was conferred with the title 'Aftab-e-Mausiqi' (Sun of Music).

questions.question: Select the Indian musician who is associated with percussion instruments (played by striking).
questions.solution:
Pandit Ayodhya Prasad was a renowned master of the Pakhawaj, which is a percussion instrument. Percussion instruments produce sound by being struck, shaken, or scraped.

Note: Other options like Pt. Ravi Shankar (Sitar) and Bismillah Khan (Shehnai) play string and wind instruments respectively.

questions.question: Which of the given musicians is associated with the musical instrument Santoor?
questions.solution:
Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is the most famous exponent of the Santoor. Through his technical innovations, he made it possible to play the complex Meend (glissando) of Indian classical music on a hammered instrument.

Recognition: He was a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan in 2001.

questions.question: M S Subbulakshmi, a legend in India is known for which of the following?
questions.solution:
M. S. Subbulakshmi was a legendary vocalist of Carnatic Music (the classical music of South India). She was the first musician ever to be awarded the Bharat Ratna.

Fact: She was also the first Indian musician to perform at the United Nations General Assembly in 1966.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian musicians is known as ‘Pancham Da’?
questions.solution:
Rahul Dev Barman (R.D. Barman) was popularly known by his nickname 'Pancham Da'. He was a revolutionary music composer in the Indian film industry, known for blending global influences like Jazz and Rock with Indian tunes.

Origin: Legend says he was called 'Pancham' because as a child, whenever he cried, it sounded like the fifth note (Pa) of the musical scale.

questions.question: Aruna Sairam, T M Krishna and Gayathri Girish are associated with which form of music?
questions.solution:
Aruna Sairam, T. M. Krishna, and Gayathri Girish are contemporary icons of Carnatic Music. This tradition is rooted in the Southern states of India and is characterized by its emphasis on Vocal compositions and complex mathematical rhythms.

Note: T.M. Krishna is also known for his social activism through art.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Benaras Gharana of Kathak?
questions.solution:
The Benaras Gharana of Kathak was founded by Janaki Prasad. This gharana is distinct because it focuses on Natwari (pure dance syllables) rather than the storytelling or erotic themes found in other schools.

Note: Ishwari Prasad is associated with the Lucknow Gharana, and Raja Chakradhar Singh founded the Raigarh Gharana.

questions.question: Ustad Hassu Khan was one of the founders of which of the following Gharanas of music?
questions.solution:
Ustad Hassu Khan, along with his brother Haddu Khan and Nathu Khan, was one of the primary founders of the Gwalior Gharana. This is considered the oldest and the mother of all Hindustani Khayal Gharanas.

Style: The Gwalior style is known for its simplicity, lucidity, and use of behalava (melodic expansion).

questions.question: Indian musician Ravi Shankar won his first Grammy Award in 1968 for best chamber music performance for which of the following works done by him?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar won his first Grammy in 1968 for the album West Meets East, a collaboration with the famous violinist Yehudi Menuhin.

Significance: This album was a milestone in global music history, as it introduced Indian classical music to the Western mainstream and established the concept of 'World Music'.
